Komotini Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Komotini, Greece

Demolished. Komotini's Jewish community, established in the early 16th century by settlers from Adrianople and Salonika, remained predominantly Sephardic and, in the 17th century, briefly hosted Nathan of Gaza, chief theologian of the Sabbatean messianic movement — the same figure associated with Kastoria's Jewish community elsewhere in this collection. During Bulgarian occupation, the community was deported to the Treblinka death camp in March 1943, unlike most Greek Jewish communities, who were sent to Auschwitz-Birkenau; postwar, only 22 Jews remained by 1948. The cemetery, presumed established in the 19th century and expanded in the 20th, was destroyed during WWII and built over between 1967 and 1974; the local Turkish quarter now occupies the site, though its exact boundaries remain uncertain even today.
